text: This scene corresponds to a standard warehouse interior environment, featuring multiple groups of large shelves, small shelves, and long shelves, along with cartons, cardboard boxes, wooden crates, plastic bins, AGVs, and mobile collaborative robots. The overall layout is centered on shelving areas and aisle areas. Some boxes are placed inside the shelves, while some boxes and wooden crates are distributed in front of the shelves or in temporary floor storage positions. The robots and AGVs are located near the warehouse transport aisles to connect the storage area and the handling area.

This scene corresponds to a relatively large automated warehousing environment, containing 6 AGVs, multiple rows of shelving, and a large quantity of boxed goods. The focus of the scene is not a single workstation, but a large shelving storage area and aisle transport area. Goods are densely distributed mainly around the shelving area, and the AGVs perform handling and circulation tasks between the aisles, making the overall layout closer to a high-density warehouse integrated with automated transport.

This scene corresponds to a warehouse environment containing shelving, boxes, and a pallet area, with 2 AGVs, multiple groups of shelving, a large number of cartons and boxed goods, as well as multiple pallets and block pallets. The overall layout combines a shelving storage area with a floor stacking area. Some goods are arranged around the shelving, while other goods and pallets are concentrated in the ground-level loading area. The AGVs are located near the warehouse aisles and the pallet area, making it suitable for describing a warehouse scene with pallet transfer and floor stacking.

This scene corresponds to a basic assembly cell, containing a factory building, 1 conveyor belt, 1 workbench, and 2 industrial robotic arms. The overall layout is organized around the workbench. The conveyor belt is positioned near the workbench to provide incoming materials, and the two robotic arms are distributed around the workbench to perform picking, placing, or assembly actions, forming a typical conveyor-fed dual-arm assembly workstation.

This scene corresponds to a multi-station assembly line, featuring 7 workbenches, 28 conveyor belts, two groups totaling 14 robotic arms, a large number of parts on the conveyor belts, parts on the workbenches, 6 AGVs, and multiple stacks of cartons. The overall spatial structure consists of multiple assembly stations arranged along the conveying line. Each area uses conveyor belts to transport parts, while robotic arms complete sorting, picking, or assembly around the workbenches. AGVs and cartons are placed along the edge of the line for material transfer and buffering.

This scene corresponds to a relatively compact assembly workspace, containing 1 workbench, 4 robotic arms, two types of parts on the workbench, 3 AGVs, and multiple stacks of cartons. Unlike a long conveyor-based assembly line, this scene emphasizes coordinated robotic-arm operations centered on a single workbench. The parts are distributed directly near the workbench, while the AGVs and cartons are placed in the peripheral area for replenishment, transfer, or buffering.

This scene corresponds to a basic sorting cell, containing an industrial building, 1 workbench, 1 robotic arm, and 1 rubber conveyor belt. The overall layout is compact. The conveyor belt is responsible for material input, the robotic arm is positioned between the conveyor belt and the workbench, and the workbench is used for classified placement or temporary storage, forming a typical single-arm short-range sorting structure.

This scene corresponds to an expanded sorting area, featuring 1 conveyor belt, 4 sorting robotic arms, 1 workbench, two types of parts on the conveyor belt, two types of parts on the workbench, 3 AGVs, and 3 stacks of cartons. The overall layout takes the form of a main conveyor line with multiple robotic arms processing in parallel. The workbench is located at the center of the sorting area, while the AGVs and stacked cartons are placed on the periphery or discharge side to receive sorted materials.

This scene corresponds to a sorting environment with dual conveyors and dual workstations, containing 2 conveyor belts, 1 sorting robotic arm, 2 workbenches, two types of parts on the conveyor belts, two types of parts on the workbenches, 3 AGVs, and 1 stack of cartons. In the overall layout, the two conveyor belts provide parallel incoming materials, the robotic arm is positioned between the conveying area and the workbench area, the two workbenches are used for temporary storage or categorized placement after sorting, and AGVs plus carton buffering positions are arranged around the periphery.

This scene corresponds to a basic palletizing cell, containing an industrial building, 2 robotic arms, 2 rubber conveyor belts, a large number of cartons, and 2 AGV docking positions. The overall structure is characterized by dual conveyor belts continuously feeding materials, robotic arms picking cartons at the ends or sides of the conveyors, and then transferring them to stacks near the docking positions, forming a typical conveyor-fed robotic palletizing layout.

This scene corresponds to a multi-channel palletizing system, featuring 8 robotic arms, 8 AGVs, 8 conveyor belts, multiple groups of boxes on the conveyor belts, and multiple stacks of cartons. The overall layout consists of multiple parallel conveying channels, with boxes continuously arriving along each channel. Robotic arms are distributed near each processing unit to complete picking and stacking, while AGVs on the discharge side or stacking side handle transfer tasks. The scene is clearly larger and more modular than the basic palletizing cell.

This scene corresponds to a high-density palletizing and transfer system, featuring two groups of robotic arms, 16 robotic arms in total, 8 AGVs, 8 conveyor belts, a large number of boxes on the conveyor belts, and multiple stacks of cartons. The overall space is structured as multiple palletizing lines running in parallel. The conveyor belts provide continuous box feeding, the two groups of robotic arms handle picking and stacking at different positions, and the AGVs are distributed around the outer side of the lines. It is suitable for describing a large-scale parallel palletizing and transfer scene.

This scene corresponds to a basic multi-station transport cell, containing a factory building, 6 conveyor belts, 6 robotic arms, 6 AGV docking positions, and 6 plastic bins. The overall layout consists of multiple similar transport modules. Each module is organized around a conveyor belt, a robotic arm, and a receiving position, while the plastic bins are placed near the docking positions to receive and transfer conveyed materials.

This scene corresponds to a long-distance continuous transport system, featuring 16 conveyor belts, 4 robotic arms, 4 AGVs, 4 cartons, and a large number of parts on the conveyor belts. The overall space is dominated by continuous conveying lines, with multiple conveyor segments connected end to end to form a long-chain transport structure. Robotic arms are distributed at several key handoff points, while AGVs and cartons are positioned alongside the line for local transfer, buffering, or discharge handling.

This scene corresponds to a mixed transfer scene, containing 1 conveyor belt, 4 robotic arms, 4 AGVs, 4 cartons, parts on the conveyor belt, parts inside the cartons, and 10 forklifts. Compared with the basic transport scene, this one includes a large number of forklifts in addition to conveyor belts and robotic arms, indicating that it covers multiple transport modes at the same time, including conveyor-line handling, box loading, and vehicle-based transfer. Overall, it is closer to a mixed internal factory logistics transfer area.
